span.label: priming works through a shift in females’ beliefs (this paper, IZA DP 4963, May 2010) → priming does not affect beliefs and works by changing preferences (the same authors' published version, Theory and Decision 2015, in this corpus as drouvelis2015-cooperation-priming)
span.note: SAME AUTHORS, SAME EXPERIMENT, OPPOSITE MECHANISM - AND THE SCHEMA HAS NO TYPE FOR IT. The 2015 paper reports two waves, the first run in 2009 with 51 and 54 subjects, which is this paper's N. So this working paper is wave one and the publication is wave one plus wave two. In wave one the raw contribution difference is NOT significant (Wilcoxon two-sided p = 0.249) and the effect appears only with a gender control at the 10% level, carried by a four-cell split of 105 subjects (19, 25, 32, 29); the mechanism is stated as two steps through female beliefs. **In the pooled publication the raw difference IS significant (p = 0.044 one-sided), there is `insufficient evidence to suggest that the effect of priming varies significantly across ... gender`, and `priming does not affect subjects' beliefs`, which is precisely what licenses its claim that priming works through PREFERENCES.** So the whole two-step belief mechanism, and the gender effect that motivated it, are absent from the published version of the same experiment. Neither paper is being called wrong here: more data arrived and a subgroup result did not survive it. What the corpus can record is that both statements exist, that they are by the same authors about the same data plus more, and where each one is. `superseded-by` / `revised-in` is the type this needs and the vocabulary does not have it - see Q-632 on the schema's missing relation types.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: priming - the same formal definition this group uses in the 2015 publication, taken from Hertel & Fiedler: a PROCEDURAL feature, previously activated information acting on the processing of subsequent information. The definition is what makes the import from psychology into economics arguable at all
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: priming as against framing - separated in a FOOTNOTE, and the distinction is the same one the 2015 paper puts in its main text: framing re-describes a logically equivalent decision problem; priming activates stored knowledge and leaves the problem alone
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: revealed preferences, as used here - the actual tokens handed over in a one-shot public good game, offered as the behavioural counterpart to the self-reported emotions

span.label: how priming works, in THIS paper's own words - a two-step chain through beliefs, stated as a finding about the female subsample: primes move what females expect others to give, and that expectation moves what they give. The 2015 publication of the same experiment reports no belief effect and attributes the result to preferences instead

span.note: depends on: a gender control - the sentence states the result only under it · direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.7 — WEIGHTED WELL BELOW THE 2015 EDGE FOR THE SAME CLAIM, and the qualifier is why: in this wave the RAW difference is not significant (Wilcoxon two-sided p = 0.249, Kolmogorov-Smirnov p = 0.552), and the effect reaches only the 10% level once gender is added. The published version with a second wave finds it in the raw comparison.

span.label: priming —causes→ beliefs
span.note: holds when: in the female subsample - the sentence names females as the ones whose beliefs shift · strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak — THE FIRST STEP OF THIS PAPER'S MECHANISM, AND THE ONE THE 2015 PUBLICATION CONTRADICTS: there, priming does not affect beliefs at all, and that null is what licenses the preferences claim. See the unhoused_relations row on this record.

span.label: Solving a word-search puzzle seeded with cooperation words raised voluntary contributions to a one-shot public good once subjects' gender was controlled for.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The raw treatment difference in mean contributions was not statistically significant, so the priming effect only emerges once composition is controlled for.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The effect was concentrated in women: positively primed females contributed about 3.25 tokens more than neutrally primed females, whereas priming did not move male contributions.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Primed women expected more from their partners than primed men did, believing the other two group members would contribute 9.52 tokens against 6.44 tokens.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Within each treatment a subject's own contribution rose with what that subject believed others would contribute, the association being slightly tighter under priming.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Priming shifted self-reported positive emotions (significantly so when partners contributed at least as much as the subject) but left negative emotions unchanged.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Full cooperators contributing the whole 20-token endowment appeared only in the primed treatment, at 13 per cent, and were absent from the neutral treatment.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In both treatments the most common contribution choices were the extremes of giving nothing or giving half the endowment.
